How it works

Your course, your materials, one clear plan.

Plaeta does not come loaded with someone else's notes. It learns your course from the documents you already have.

01

Add your subjects and syllabus

Upload the syllabus for each subject. Plaeta lists its topics and dot points so you can tick them off as you learn them.

02

Add your study materials

Drag in past papers with their marking guidelines or solutions, plus your notes and handouts. Every question is read, sorted into topics and ready to practise.

03

Answer, get marked, improve

Type or photograph your answer for a mark against the criteria and clear feedback. Your flashcards, mistake logbook and daily timetable then keep you working on what needs it.

Get the highlights

What each part is for.

Timetable

A plan for every day, built around your week.

Set your free times and exam dates once. Each day you get study blocks with homework first, and the Sun shares your week between your subjects.

Focus

Sit down, pick a time, start.

Choose how long you have and what to work on. Plaeta builds a set of questions from your own papers that fills exactly that time.

Notes

Notes for every topic.

Write notes topic by topic, with maths and photos of your working. You can see which topics still have no notes, and Quiz me tests you on any note.

Essay lab

Timed writing, marked to criteria.

Pick the kind of writing, paste in the question and write against the clock. Varda marks it against your own criteria, or general ones clearly labelled as not official.

My texts

Your set texts in one place.

Keep your own copies of the texts you study and your teacher's handouts. The text tutor, quote finder and question maker read them when you ask.

Logbook and flashcards

Turn lost marks into practice.

Write a one-line rule each time you lose a mark, then test yourself on your rules. Flashcards come from your own lists and from questions you lost marks on.

Syllabus and assessments

Know what is covered, and what is coming up.

Tick off topics as your class covers them, so practice only comes from what you have learnt. Add assessment tasks and your teacher's marks to see how you are tracking.

Example app

Try it out for yourself.

A working example of the app with made-up subjects and data. Pick a subject, make an example paper and answer a question. Nothing you type is saved or leaves this page, and no AI is used here.

Marking you can check

Feedback that shows where the marks went.

Each answer is marked against the guidelines that came with the paper, criterion by criterion, so you can see what earned marks and what was missing.

  • Every question can be marked. No caps per paper. Essay marking has a monthly fair-use limit.
  • Clearly labelled as AI. Check it against your criteria, and ask your teacher when unsure.
  • Mistakes become practice. Weak topics feed your flashcards and your study plan.
Modern HistoryPractice paper · Q14
Question 14 · 4 marks

Explain two causes of the economic collapse described in Source B.

Source B shows that falling crop prices left farmers unable to repay loans, which caused rural banks to fail…
Identifies two relevant causes2 / 2
Explains each with evidence from the source1 / 2
3out of 4AI-marked
To get the last mark: link your second cause to a detail in the source, such as the figures for bank closures.
Built for each subject

Every subject studies differently.

Plaeta sets up each subject for how it is examined, so maths feels like maths and English feels like English.

Maths

Standard, Advanced and beyond

  • Marks your working, step by step
  • Formula sheets kept by topic
  • Similar questions to retry

English

Standard, Advanced and more

  • Essay lab and essay planner
  • Quote bank and notes for your texts
  • Question maker for any module

Humanities

History, Business, Religion

  • Source analysis practice
  • Extended responses marked to criteria

Sciences

Biology, Chemistry, Health

  • Calculations and data questions

Any other subject works too. Languages get a vocabulary list and grammar notes. Subjects like Multimedia, Industrial Technology, Visual Arts and Music get the core tools: notes, flashcards and past papers marked to your criteria.

Questions

Good to know.

Which courses does Plaeta work with?
Any Year 11 and 12 course with a syllabus. You upload your own syllabus and study materials, so Plaeta follows exactly what your course covers, whichever state you study in.
Does Plaeta come with past papers?
No. You upload the papers you have, from your teachers, your school or your own collection, along with their marking guidelines or solutions. Plaeta marks against those.
Does Plaeta cost anything?
No. Plaeta is free to use, with every feature included. To keep it free for everyone, each student has a monthly limit on past paper uploads and essay marking. You can see how much you have used in Settings.
What counts as a paper?
One uploaded exam or practice paper counts as one paper, at the moment you upload it. Every question in it can be marked, as many times as you like.
What happens to my papers after 60 days?
The paper file and its question text are deleted automatically. Your own answers, marks, feedback, flashcards and progress stay in your account.
Can AI marking be wrong?
Yes, sometimes. Every AI mark is labelled, and it is always measured against the criteria you uploaded. Use it to practise and check it against your criteria. Your teacher's marks always come first.
Who can sign up?
Plaeta is made for students aged about 16 to 18. You enter your date of birth when you sign up. If you are under 18, a parent or carer should read the terms with you.
